item.title: 30 years of the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health (ALSWH)
item.description:
Wednesday, 5 August 2026

Reddacliff Place sculptures will be lit Purple to celebrate 30 years of the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health (ALSWH)

This year, the Australian Women and Girls’ Health Research Centre (AWaGR), University of Queensland (UQ), and Centre for Women’s Health Research (CWHR), University of Newcastle (UON) will celebrate 30 years of the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health (ALSWH). This is the largest and longest-running national study of women’s health and wellbeing, taking from over 57,000 Australian women in four cohorts. Established in 1996, their data provides invaluable information about the health of women across the lifespan and ensures the country’s health policy for women is based on strong data.

This Light Up is organised by: Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health

Venue address: Reddacliff Place, 266 George Street, Brisbane City
Venue type: General Council venue, Light up asset

item.title: National Eosinophilic Week
item.description:
Saturday, 8 August 2026

City Hall will be lit Pink and Purple to support National Eosinophilic Week

National Eosinophilic Week (NEOSW) will be celebrated nationally from 2-8 August 2026. Eosinophils are a type of white blood cell and NEOSW aims to increase awareness and understanding in the community about eosinophil-associated diseases including eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases (EGIDs). ausEE Inc. is Australia’s peak national support and patient advocacy organisation representing people living with an eosinophilic disease including eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases (EGIDs). As a registered charity our mission is to improve the lives of those affected by eosinophilic diseases through providing support, evidence-based information, resources, advocacy and by campaigning to raise awareness and funds for research in Australia.

This Light Up is organised by: ausEE

item.title: Ekka
item.description:
Sunday, 9 August 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Green to celebrate Ekka

Ekka - 150 Years in the Making!
In 2026, the Ekka celebrates an incredible milestone - 150 years of bringing Queenslanders together for the state’s biggest and most loved event. Staged at its original birthplace, the Brisbane Showgrounds, the Ekka has been uniting city and country since 1876 in a true celebration of agriculture and community.
Showcasing the very best of Queensland, with more than 21,000 competition entries, over 10,000 animals from cattle to cats, world-class live entertainment, award-winning food and wine, carnival rides and showbags, family shopping, educational activities and much more. For 150 years, the Ekka has been attracting more than 400,000 people each year.
Ekka will run for 9 days from the Saturday, 8th - Sunday, 16th August 2026, and includes Peoples Day on Wednesday August 12th.

This Light Up is organised by: Brisbane Economic Development Agency

item.title: Dress to Express Day
item.description:
Friday, 28 August 2026

City Hall will be lit Purple and Orange to support Dress to Express Day

Dress to Express is a primary prevention initiative, in partnership with Brisbane Fashion Festival (our fourth year). The focus is twofold- to support and celebrate DV survivors who are rediscovering their own identity and style and to educate the community about the subtle signs of coercive control through something we can all relate to - fashion. We will walk in solidarity from King George Square to the Queen St Mall stage where there will be a rally with music, speakers and info stalls

This Light Up is organised by: Beyond DV
